answer: A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Policies are written in atlas, settled in mirror, and marble lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 20% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. That bill is paid per identity, so 230 aliases cost 341 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
